title: Eleven Lines in a Dictionary
subtitle: 词语与用法 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 词语与用法（语言与思维·词汇与语义）
meta: 主题语境：词语与用法（语言与思维·词汇与语义）　|　核心词汇：communist　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 communist 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1951 my great-aunt ① looked up the word communist in a dictionary she had borrowed, and she said the looking was the whole of the lesson. The ② communist, meaning the entry and not the person, ran to eleven lines and stayed that length for years; communist, she said, is the only word in a dictionary that is judged by how often it is looked up.

Every ③ communist in that dictionary had the same few lines, and the ④ communist at the end, meaning the one printed in the appendix and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever copied twice. Communist, my grandmother said, is nine parts print and one part somebody willing to look; my great-aunt said the looking is the part that wears the page.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the communist in the story was the whole of the chapter, meaning the character and not the entry. The ⑥ communist, meaning the character and not any of that, is the only thing in a chapter that everybody discusses and nobody defines; communist, he said, is either something you look up or the only word that means both an entry and a character. She said the character is the part they remember.

By 1959 the ⑦ communist had become a line in a bibliography, and the bibliography had become an argument about sources. The ⑧ communist of the whole thing, my great-aunt wrote in April, was one entry and thirty years of looking; communist, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to check a source. He said the checking was never mentioned.

The ⑨ communist I remember is the one at the end, which was printed in 1963 and is still described as the shortest in the appendix. A ⑩ communist, my grandmother said in 1965, is the only word that improves by being checked; every communist, she said, is a character that has agreed to look like an entry. She said the character was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 共产主义者；共产党员
B. n. 该词（指词典里的那条词条本身，与那个人相对）
C. 固定搭配：look up the word communist 查这个词
D. n. 该词（指那本词典里每一条）
E. n. 该词（指末尾那一条）
F. n. 该词（指小说里的那个人物）
G. n. 该词（指文献目录里提到的那一条）
H. n. 该词的用法（抽象总称）

items.q: looked up the word communist in a dictionary
The communist, meaning the entry and not the person
the communist in the story was the whole of the chapter
the communist had become a line in a bibliography
The communist of the whole thing
A communist, my grandmother said in 1965

answers.why: look up the word 意为“查这个词”，1951 年姑祖母在一本借来的词典里查了 communist 这个词。
communist 在这里指词典里的那条词条本身，而不是那个人，它有十一行那么长。
communist 指那本词典里每一条同形词条，每一条都只有寥寥几行。
communist 指末尾那一条（印在附录里的那一条），是唯一有人抄过两次的。
communist 指小说里的那个人物，父亲说这个人物就是那一章的全部，而不是那个词条。
communist 为语境用法，指书中的人物而不是那个词条，是章节里人人讨论、却无人下定义的东西。
communist 指文献目录里提到的那一条，到 1959 年这个词成了文献目录里的一行。
communist 指该词的用法，姑祖母四月写道，整件事关于这个词的用法是一条词条三十年的查阅。
communist 意为“共产主义者、共产党员”，我记得的是末尾那一条，1963 年印出，至今仍被说成附录里最短的。
communist 为抽象总称，祖母说这个词是唯一会因为被核对而变好的东西。

那条词条，指的是那条词条本身而不是那个人，有十一行那么长，并且多年来一直是那个长度。（communist）
那本词典里每一条同形词条都只有寥寥几行。（communist）
末尾那一条，指的是印在附录里的那一条，是唯一有人抄过两次的。（communist）
父亲说这个人物就是那一章的全部，指的是书中的人物而不是那条词条。（communist）
1965 年祖母说，这个词是唯一会因为被核对而变好的东西。（communist）

The communist, meaning the entry and not the person, ran to eleven lines and stayed that length for years.
Every communist in that dictionary had the same few lines.
The communist at the end, meaning the one printed in the appendix and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever copied twice.
My father said the communist in the story was the whole of the chapter, meaning the character and not the entry.
